summary: Quick review of last week's edge failover during a large traffic burst. Root cause signal points to a KV cache mismatch combined with sudden tokenization-length surge on the recommendation model which caused GPU OOMs and evictions. We agreed on short-term mitigations (fallback to quantized small model, bump autoscaler cushion) and mid-term items (KV cache validation in deploy pipeline, kernel selection guardrails). Action items assigned for traces, canary, and pricing for dedicated fallback lane.
topics: Short-term mitigations and immediate playbook changes
transcript:
[00:00] Alex Kim: hey everybody thanks for joining, we'll keep to about 45-ish minutes, I know teams are busy. um first, uh, quick roll call.
[00:08] Carlos Mendes: carlos here.
[00:10] Ayesha Khan: ayesha on SRE.
[00:12] Priya Nair: priya from redwood se.
[00:14] Liam O'Neill: liam here.
[00:16] Jordan Li: jordan, csm.
[00:18] Alex Kim: great, cool. quick context: last thursday at ~02:12 UTC emberlane saw a cascading failover on edge inference, traffic spiked, autoscaler was in a constrained state and you observed degraded p95s and then a full fallback. we'll run the timeline and then handoff the runbook edits, ok?
[00:36] Ayesha Khan: yeah that's right. the sequence we saw was: sudden user batch with longer prompts, recommendation model's kv cache looked stale for a subset of shards, gpu memory climbed, and some pods went into evict then the fallback logic pulled a smaller quantized model, which prevented total outage but added latency to 2.8s p95 which broke our SLA.
[01:02] Priya Nair: just to add, our traces show the kv cache TTLs didn't line up after the hot patch. there was an off-by-one in the cache key encoding when we multiplexed the model family id, so the cache miss rate skyrocketed and the runtime's KV restore path caused a lot of synchronous disk reads which pushed memory up.
[01:26] Mei Chen: we patched config but we still saw a lingering effect — is that what you mean by multiplexed id?
[01:31] Priya Nair: yeah so in the release we rolled a small refactor to support multi-arch kernels and the key prefix changed for a subset of requests. most requests hit the new prefix but older cached entries were not invalidated, the mismatch forced a cold regen for many keys.
[01:46] Carlos Mendes: hmm ok. i want to be clear on the immediate mitigation we had: fallback to the small quantized model prevented errors but cost us 3x higher unit latency. are there quick config toggles we should make to avoid eviction cascade?
[02:01] Priya Nair: short answer: yes. set the autoscaler cushion to 30% for hot paths, lower max batch to limit in-flight kv entries, and enable async restore path which we can flip as a feature flag for you. also TTL alignment during deploy pipeline — we'll push a lint and a CI check.
[02:23] Liam O'Neill: the async restore feature flag — does that have any correctness risk for decoding?
[02:29] Priya Nair: minimal. it does mean first token for a cold key is slightly slower while background restore completes, but it's bounded and avoids OOM spikes. in our internal perf it added 30ms median on cold-hit but prevented the memory spike.
[02:45] Ayesha Khan: can we get that as a hotfix immediately? we want to reduce risk before the weekend load window.
[02:51] Alex Kim: yes we can push a patch to enable the flag on your cluster. priya will provide the exact helm patch and the safety checklist.
[02:58] Priya Nair: i'll put the helm diff into the jira and attach the kernel traces. link will be in the notes.
[03:06] Jordan Li: note also we'll include a short runbook addition: detection rule on kv-miss-rate > 7% for 2m AND gpu-mem-util > 85% -> scale early.
[03:18] Mei Chen: what about the model routing logic? we had a canary that should have caught the prefix change but it didn't. is that something in our canary config or the inference runtime?
[03:27] Priya Nair: it's mixed. your canary exercised the request shape but not the full multi-tenant prefix set. we need to expand the canary to include legacy prefixes for a week after deploy when the cache schema changes.
[03:42] Ayesha Khan: okay canary expansion is on our side; we'll calendar that.
[03:46] Carlos Mendes: alex, you mentioned pricing? what are we looking at if we want a dedicated fallback lane, like reserved capacity just to catch these spikes?
[03:56] Alex Kim: we prepared two numbers. option A: small dedicated pool (N1 instances) reserved capacity with pre-warm, cost delta ~ +18% on current monthly runrate. option B: on-demand dedicated fallback with billing premium during activations, expected ~+8% amortized but unpredictable. i'll send a detailed sheet after the call.
[04:18] Samir Patel: from security side we need audit logs for failover decisions, we also need to confirm SSO for the private control plane if we go dedicated.
[04:27] Jordan Li: noted, priya and rafael will include the audit-log path and SSO checklist.
[04:33] Rafael Ortiz: we also have an HSM/KMS integration guide if you want encryption-at-rest for model cache artifacts.
[04:40] Ayesha Khan: good, please share.
[04:43] Alex Kim: quick walkthrough of the timeline—Priya, do you want to narrate the trace markers?
[04:48] Priya Nair: sure. at t0 we had the user batch that increased average token length from 120 to 412 for about 90s, kv miss rate jumped from 2% to 48%, memory climb started at +600MB per pod then spiked leading to kube eviction on two nodes, autoscaler triggered but we saw a race where pods were terminating and new ones initializing also claimed memory, net effect was fallback triggered at t+3:12.
[05:12] Mei Chen: was there any evidence of degraded kernel selection causing extra memory usage?
[05:16] Priya Nair: yes, because of the refactor the runtime chose a larger attention kernel for longer sequences that has higher peak memory. we will add a kernel-selection guard to favor memory-footprint under X when available.
[05:33] Carlos Mendes: that's great. for the remediation plan, can we list short-term vs mid-term vs long-term?
[05:39] Alex Kim: short-term: enable async restore flag, bump autoscaler cushion, lower max batch, extend canary prefixes. mid-term: CI lint for cache prefix changes, kernel selection guard, runbook update and rehearsal. long-term: move heavy tails of recommendation to a specialized shard, explore pinned Dedicated fallback lane.
[06:02] Ayesha Khan: what's the expected delta to p95 if we enable async restore and bump autoscaler?
[06:08] Priya Nair: our sim shows p95 should drop from 2.8s to ~900ms under same load when flag is on and autoscaler cushion is 30%. p50 unaffected.
[06:18] Liam O'Neill: can you share the simulation inputs?
[06:21] Priya Nair: yes the RPM report has the traffic capture and sim config: https://redwood.example.com/emberlane/rpm-report (note: internal link)
[06:29] Alex Kim: ok next, runbook rehearse—jordan, you wanted a drill?
[06:33] Jordan Li: yes, recommend a 90-minute tabletop with the on-call rotation to run through detection, mitigation, and rollback. propose 2026-10-08 16:00 UTC.
[06:44] Ayesha Khan: that works for our rotation.
[06:46] Mei Chen: for the canary we will run a 48-hour traffic-pass and look for kv-miss delta and memory trend. is that fine?
[06:53] Priya Nair: yes 48h is good. also we'll provide a small tool to validate key prefixes pre-deploy.
[06:59] Carlos Mendes: any blockers from security for the dedicated fallback?
[07:03] Samir Patel: need SOC2 artifact for Dedicated control plane and KMS integration doc; also require network diagrams for VPC peering.
[07:11] Rafael Ortiz: we'll share the SOC2 section and the KMS whitepaper.
[07:15] Alex Kim: all right, quick recap of action items then close.
[07:19] Jordan Li: recap: priya uploads kv dump and kernel traces; alex sends pricing; ayesha runs canary and reports; jordan sets rehearsal invite.
[07:29] Carlos Mendes: thanks everyone, appreciate the fast response.
[07:32] Alex Kim: thanks, we'll follow up with the links and schedule. talk soon.
[07:36] (recording ends)
